item.title: Road Safety Report(Southbury Road and Fotherigham Road, 9th October
item.description:
Dear Enfield Council Highways Department, I am writing to formally report a serious public safety hazard regarding the restricted bus lane on Fotheringham Road, located just off Southbury Road (past the Tesco store) as you drive down from Enfield Town towards Great Cambridge Road. This is the specific restricted section where only the 192 bus is permitted to enter by turning right from the main road. I am a local resident, living on Seaforth Road, just 50 metres away from this restricted road. I am fully aware of the restrictions, I never turn into this street, and I always use the next road, Cecil Road, instead to get to my house. However, on Thursday 8th October, between 9:30 PM and 10:00 PM, during heavy rainfall, the driving conditions at this junction became extremely hazardous and misleading due to the following reasons: 1. As I was driving down Southbury Road, when there is a bus stopped in such a section of the road, it completely blocks the advance warning signs located on the left side of Southbury Road which indicate that private vehicles cannot turn right. With the signage completely hidden, I was forced to make a small bypass to the right to clear the bus, under the impression that the turning right ahead of me was Cecil Road. 2. At the same time, from the oncoming direction (driving up Southbury Road from Great Cambridge Road towards Enfield Town), other buses, lorries, and cars were approaching, and their headlights in the dark and rain created severe visibility issues. 3. I was waiting for the oncoming vehicles to pass before making the right turn. However, at the exact moment they passed, their large physical profile completely blocked the view of the restriction signs located on both the right and left sides at the entrance of Fotheringham Road. As a result, I turned without realising, while driving on Southbury Road, because I thought I was making the turn for Cecil Road (a situation which, from what I have asked, happens to other drivers as well, and as I have personally observed at various other times, other drivers frequently make the exact same mistake). Due to the reflection of the rain on the road surface, the darkness, and the blinding lights on one side, combined with the hidden signs on the other, it is very easy under these conditions for certain drivers to make a wrong decision at that instant. Therefore, despite being completely familiar with the area, I made an unintentional turn. As soon as I entered slightly and realised it was not Cecil Road, I immediately turned on my hazard lights and safely reversed out. I trust that no Penalty Charge Notice will be issued, as the camera footage will verify that I immediately reversed out upon realising the situation. From what I know and from speaking with my neighbours, this problem happens to quite a few drivers. In fact, many drivers (such as visitors or strangers coming to see residents in the neighbourhood who almost never travel on this road) do not even realise their mistake. I kindly request that, if possible, the Council reviews this specific location to see if there is a way to improve the current conditions and visibility, in order to prevent motorists from making this mistake in the first place. Note that in my many years of driving and having spent thousands of hours on the road, either driving or as a passenger on a bus, I very rarely remember observing or encountering a car entering in this manner. However, I have noticed that on this specific road, some people occasionally enter against the restrictions, exactly as happened to me. In fact, when they meet cars coming from the other side, they are alerted that it is a mistake, and they look surprised because they had not realised it at all. Yours faithfully, Kostas Maroulis, 22B Seaforth Road, 34 Felix House, Enfield EN1 1NT
Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Southbury Road, Enfield
